evidence.excerpt: Seal-initiation temperature (SIT) is a primary determinant of packaging line throughput on vertical form–fill–seal machines. This work compared cast films produced from four mLLDPE resins differing in comonomer type (1-butene, 1-hexene, or 1-octene) at constant density (0.918 g/cm³) and melt flow index (2.0 g/10 min). Films of 40 µm nominal thickness were extruded on a laboratory cast-film line and sealed over a 90–135 °C range at 0.3 N/mm² and 0.5 s dwell time. Seal strength was measured by 180° peel on a tensile tester. The 1-octene grade yielded the lowest SIT (97 °C) and a plateau seal strength of 28 N/25 mm, compared to 108 °C and 22 N/25 mm for the 1-butene grade. DSC melting profiles correlated well with the observed SIT differences. Hot-tack measurements at 500 mm/s jaw separation confirmed that 1-octene resins provide a 14 °C wider hot-tack window, relevant for high-speed filling lines.
